label: Delimiter in short sequences, plus first q/g/2 early in the input
explanation: Fires only before the copy phase, never at t=0/1 or during copying. About half the activation mass is at the <DEL> step: 27% of delimiters fire, more often for short sequences (L=3-4 most) and when the sequence starts with m/k/r/a. These include the strongest activations (e.g. m m c <DEL>). The other half is in the original phase at t=2..6, almost entirely on first occurrences of a token, with a strong preference for q (24% rate), digit 2, and g; c/n/0 fire weakly. Rate falls off sharply after t=6. Magnitude is largest at the delimiter of short sequences beginning with m/k. Token identity and position only partly determine firing, so precision stays moderate (dev F1 about 0.59, mass recall about 0.80).
